title: Ligand-directed labeling of opioid receptors for covalent attachment of fluorophores or small-molecule probes
protocol: Dissolve succinic anhydride in 15 mL of anhydrous dimethylformamide (DMF) under an argon atmosphere.
Add a solution of histamine·2HCl and triethylamine dropwise to the stirred succinic anhydride solution.
Stir the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature.
Filter the reaction mixture through a fritted glass funnel using a house vacuum.
Discard precipitate.
Collect filtrate into a round bottom flask.
Remove DMF from the filtrate under reduced pressure.
Dissolve residue in ethanol.
Chill the mixture to 4°C overnight in a cold room or fridge.
Filter the cloudy solution using a fritted glass funnel placed on a filtering flask and apply a house vacuum to filter.
Wash the solid product three times with ice-cold ethanol by adding solvent to the precipitate in the fritted glass funnel and applying a house vacuum to remove ethanol.
Place the wet solid product in a 20 mL scintillation vial.
Dry the solid product by applying a house or high vacuum at room temperature.
Dissolve compound 1 in 1 mL DMF, add HBTU and triethylamine, stir for 30 min at room temperature.
Dissolve β-naltrexamine·2HCl in 0.5 mL DMF.
Transfer the naltrexamine solution to a 2.5 mL microwave vial.
Add the compound 1 solution from step a to the vial.
Add another 1 mL DMF to wash down the reagents on the side of the vial.
Set a Biotage Initiator+ Microwave Reactor to 150°C, 10 min reaction time at normal absorption.
Check completion of the reaction by HPLC analysis using reverse phase Vydac 300Å C8 column with linear gradient from 0%–40% acetonitrile in water with 0.1% formic acid over 15 minutes.
Pour the reaction mixture into a round bottom flask.
Remove DMF under reduced pressure by applying vacuum using Fisher Scientific Maxima C Plus high vac pump connected to a condensing device for liquid collection.
Dissolve the residue, which appears as a film around the round bottom flask with 5% acetonitrile in water plus 0.1% formic acid for HPLC purification.
Purify the crude solution with an Agilent 1260 Infinity II semi-preparative HPLC system.
Use a reverse phase Vydac 300Å C8, 10 × 250 mm column.
Maintain a flow rate of 5 mL/min.
Apply a linear gradient over 25 min from 0% to 40% acetonitrile in water with 0.1% formic acid.
Combine pure fractions obtained from the purification.
Lyophilize the combined pure fractions.
Obtain a lyophilized, white powder at approximately 94% yield of starting material and purity of 97% as determined by HPLC.
Take 10 mg of compound 2 and dissolve in deuterated methanol for NMR analysis.
Analyze the dissolved sample using an Agilent 1260 Infinity II analytical HPLC equipped with a Thermo Scientific Velos LTQ mass spectrometer.
Use reverse phase Agilent Pursuit XRs 100Å C18, 4.6 × 250 mm column, and a linear gradient from 0% to 40% acetonitrile in water with 0.1% formic acid at 1 mL/min flow.
Observe the product peak at m/z+1 of 536.5 on the electron-spray ionized mass spectrum for compound 2.
Perform NMR analysis using a 1HNMR (400 MHz, CD3OD) to confirm the purity and structure of compound 2.
Recover material used for NMR analyses by removing deuterated methanol under reduced pressure.
Dissolve 2-(Prop-2-yn-1-yloxy)ethanol (25.0 mg, 0.25 mmol) and triethylamine (140 μL, 1 mmol) in 3 mL acetonitrile.
Heat the mixture to 40°C while stirring using a magnetic bar and stirrer/hotplate.
Add N,N′-disuccinimidyl carbonate (96 mg, 0.375 mmol) and continue stirring for 2 h at 40°C.
Check completion of reaction by thin-layer chromatography (TLC).
Remove acetonitrile under reduced pressure on a Heidolph rotary evaporator.
Dissolve the crude oil in dichloromethane (DCM) for purification.
Purify with silica gel chromatography using a Biotage ZIP KP-Sil 10 g column and stepwise gradient of ethyl acetate/hexane.
Check fractions for product mass by Flow Injection Mass Spectrometry.
Combine eluent fractions containing the product.
Remove solvent under reduced pressure using a Heidolph rotary evaporator.
Dissolve 10 mg of light-yellow oil in deuterated chloroform for NMR analysis.
Store compound 3 at -20°C for up to 3 months.
Dissolve compound 3 (7 mg, 29 μmol) in 1.7 ml anhydrous DMF.
Add compound 2 (13 mg, 24 μmol) and 3 μL anhydrous pyridine.
Stir the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature under an argon atmosphere.
Remove the solvent under reduced pressure using a Fisher Scientific Maxima C Plus high vac pump connected to a condensing device for liquid collection.
Dissolve residue in 10% ACN in water with 0.1% formic acid (FA).
Purify the crude mixture with an Agilent semi-preparative HPLC system using a reverse phase Agilent Pursuit XRs 100Å C18 column, 10 × 250 mm.
Run purification at 5 mL/min flow and linear gradient over 25 min from 5% to 60% acetonitrile in water with 0.1% formic acid.
Combine pure fractions obtained during HPLC purification.
Lyophilize the combined fractions.
Check purity of lyophilized powder using Agilent 1260 Infinity II analytical HPLC connected to a Thermo Scientific Velos LIQ mass spectrometer.
Use reverse phase Agilent Pursuit XRs 100Å C18, 4.6 × 250 mm column for analysis at 1 mL/min flow rate.
Analyze using linear gradient over 15 min from 5% to 60% acetonitrile in water with 0.1% formic acid.
Monitor product peak appearing at 662.1 (m/z+1) on the electron-spray ionized mass spectrum.
Simultaneously monitor UV absorption at 218 nm during analysis.
Detect retention time of the product at 9.7 min for identification and purity assessment.
Obtain lyophilized, white powder at approximately 25% yield with 97% purity determined by HPLC.
Take approximately 1 mg of solid powder and dissolve it in deuterium methanol for NMR analysis.
Store compound 4 in a moisture-controlled container at -80°C.
Use compound 4 promptly in the next step.
Dissolve Alexa594 azide (1 mg, 1.16 μmol) in 450 μL anhydrous dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO).
Add tris(benzyltriazolylmethyl)amine (TBTA, 19 mg, 36 μmol) to the solution.
Add tetrakis(acetonitrile)copper(I) tetrafluoroborate (Cu[MeCN]4BF4, 8 mg, 27 μmol) to the mixture.
Dissolve compound 4 in 450 mL anhydrous DMSO.
Add the solution to a mixture under argon.
Stir the mixture overnight (12–18 hours).
Check completion of the reaction by HPLC analysis.
Purify the reaction mixture on an Agilent Infinity preparative HPLC.
Combine pure fractions and lyophilize overnight (12–18 hours).
Check the purity of the lyophilized powder using HPLC and mass spectrometry.
Connect an Agilent 1260 Infinity II analytical HPLC to a Thermo Scientific Velos LTQ mass spectrometer.
Use a reverse phase Agilent Pursuit XRs 100Å C18 column, 4.6 × 250 mm.
Run the sample at 1 mL/min flow with a linear gradient from 5%–60% acetonitrile in water containing 0.1% formic acid over 15 min.
Monitor product peak at m/z+2 on the mass spectrum (755.46).
Use UV absorption to monitor the product at wavelengths of 220 and 594 nm.
Dissolve lyophilized product in ∼2 mL acetonitrile/water (1:1) with 0.1% formic acid if necessary.
Dilute 10 μL sample with 990 μL methanol.
Measure absorbance at 590 nm.
Calculate concentration using c = (A/(εL))∗f, where A is the absorbance, ε is the extinction coefficient (88000 M-1 cm-1), L is light path length in cm, and f is dilution factor.
If absorbance is above 1, make a new dilution until absorbance is below or in the linear range of Beer’s Law.
Aliquot 20 nmol portions and lyophilize.
Store small aliquots of 20 nmol dried compound at -20°C with humidity control.
Seed 3 × 10^5 cells stably expressing μ-opioid receptors (MOR) into various wells of a 12 well plate.
Seed an additional well of cells to serve as a background control labeled NAI-X in the presence of excess naloxone, 10 μM.
Return cells to incubator set to 37°C, 93% humidity, and 5% CO2 for 48 h to grow to ∼1 × 10^6 in number (70% confluence).
Once cells have reached desired confluence, add a final concentration of 10 μM naloxone to all background control wells.
Add a range of concentrations (10–500 nM) of NAI-X to control and test wells.
Return cells to incubator at 37°C, 93% humidity, and 5% CO2.
Allow labeling to proceed for 1 h.
Once labeling is completed, wash each well once with PBS.
Aspirate PBS and add 500 μL of TrypLE to lift cells.
Incubate at room temperature for 4 min or 37°C for 2 min.
Add 1 mL of Gibco™ High-Glucose DMEM with 10% FBS.
Gently pipette up and down four times without introducing air bubbles to ensure all cells are lifted from the treated surface of the flask.
Transfer cells to Eppendorf tubes.
Spin down cells in Eppendorf tubes at 300 × g for 2 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS with 10 μM naloxone.
Add naloxone to remove unreacted NAI-X from the orthosteric binding site on the receptor.
Ensure the fluorescent signal is only from NAI-X that has undergone covalent labeling.
Analyze samples by flow cytometry, capturing 10,000 events after gating for single cells.
Plate cells on imaging dishes for live cell imaging studies.
Seed 3 × 10^4 cells per well (∼10% confluence) in LabTek II 8 well dishes with borosilicate glass bottoms.
Culture cells until they reach approximately 40%-60% confluent.
Incubate cells with 400 nM NAI-A488 for varying time points to monitor labeling saturation.
Include naloxone at a concentration of 10 μM in the solution of NAI-A488 to demonstrate negligible background fluorescence.
Warm media to 37°C in incubator two days later.
Coat LabTek II 8 well dishes with poly-L-lysine following manufacturer’s instructions.
Wash cells twice with pre-equilibrated media (DMEM without phenol red, supplemented with 20 mM HEPES).
Add NAI-A488 to well(s) at 400 nM.
Return cells to incubator to label for 10 min.
Replace media with fresh pre-equilibrated media after washing cells.
Image on microscope (Nikon Spinning Disk confocal with temperature control at 37°C, 100× objective, 2-s exposure per image).
Monitor agonist-induced receptor endocytosis on microscope.
Prepare brain slices as shown in the "before you begin" section.
Incubate brain slices with NAI-X for labeling opioid receptors.
Maintain healthy brain slices during labeling using an incubation vial.
Fix labeled slices for further study after labeling.
Prepare a 10-mL syringe and cut the tip near the 3 mL mark.
Stretch a small piece of mesh fabric over the opening of the syringe.
Secure the mesh fabric with a rubber band.
Use cyanoacrylate glue to fix the mesh fabric to the barrel of the syringe.
Cut and remove excess fabric material.
Prepare a 30-mL scintillation vial as an incubating container.
Add 4 mL ACSF buffer into the scintillation vial.
Insert a small tube for bubbling carbogen gas outside the net chamber.
Add 4 μL of NAI-X to the vial, mixing well (NAI-X concentration is 100 nM).
Drop a single brain slice inside the net chamber without stacking slices on top of each other.
Incubate the brain slices for 1 hour at 30°C–34°C.
Be careful not to cause brain slices to swirl during this step.
Submerge a labeled slice under ACSF in a petri dish.
Visualize labeled receptors on large brain areas using a macroscope.
Use naloxone to confirm specific labeling of ORs when included in the NAI-A594 labeling solution.
Submerge brain slices in continuous flow of oxygenated ACSF at 34°C.
Take labeled slice to a 2-photon microscope to visualize labeled receptors on neuron.
Use a 60× water immersion lens and laser at 810 nm excitation for imaging.
Incubate brain slices in oxygenated ACSF containing NAI-X at a final concentration of 30 or 100 nM for 1 h at 30°C–34°C.
Wash labeled slices twice with 2 × 10 mL ACSF.
Add 4% formaldehyde to labeled slices in Petri Dish.
Shake slices in a Petri dish using a rotator for 20 min.
Wash fixed slices in saline-phosphate buffer twice.
